Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., disclosed that the company has dropped its lawsuit against him, which was filed in response to his challenge of the validity of the company's 70% supermajority bylaw. This move comes after the Texas Business Court ordered Fermi to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw, and Neugebauer claims that the company's decision to abandon the lawsuit confirms that the bylaw was adopted to entrench the board's power. Neugebauer's claims challenging the validity of the bylaw remain alive and he will continue to pursue discovery and depositions of key players.

general.summary: Samsung Electronics plans shareholder returns totaling 90 trillion won to 110 trillion won, including about 30 trillion won in third-quarter cash dividends.

general.title: Euro-Area Pay Growth Eased in Second Quarter, ECB Says
general.summary: A key measure of euro-area pay growth eased, offering further relief to the European Central Bank as it assesses inflation risks from the Iran war.

general.title: South Korea, Japan FX Officials Vow to Deepen Cooperation
general.summary: South Korea and Japan’s top foreign-exchange officials met in Tokyo on Friday to discuss ways to enhance bilateral cooperation, three weeks after a rare US-Japan coordinated intervention jolted the region’s currency markets and helped bolster the won as well as the yen.

general.title: Japan Earmarks Another $944 Million for Rapidus in AI Chip Race
general.summary: Japan’s government is allocating an additional ¥150 billion ($944 million) for chip startup Rapidus Corp., ramping up spending in a long-shot bid to compete against the likes of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.

general.title: Humanoid Robots Put China Ahead in Tech Race
general.summary: China’s humanoid robot makers now control 97% of global shipments, giving Beijing an early lead over US rivals. But can they become everyday tools? At the World Robot Conference in Beijing, robots sort boxes, handle laundry and bag clothes, as Allen Wan finds out. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Danish Businesses Most Upbeat in Four Years Despite Pharma Gloom
general.summary: Danish businesses turned the most optimistic in more than four years as stronger confidence in retail and services offset a still-gloomy mood in the industrial sector.

general.title: UK Economy Speeds Up as Firms and Shoppers Splash Out, PMI Shows
general.summary: Britain’s private sector expanded at the fastest pace in four months, as sunny weather and a strong service sector prompted households and businesses to turn on the spending taps.

general.title: What the AI Industry Got Wrong About Public Backlash
general.summary: Even those within the AI industry have been very anxious about the technology. Worries about its potential to create destabilizing job losses, or rogue AI that could lead to human extinction. But for all their anxiety, they missed the thing that's become the most publicly salient: how upset people would be about data centers. general.title: Alphabet Bond Buyer Warns on Australia’s Capacity for AI Debt
general.summary: Australian state-owned investment manager QIC Ltd., which invested in Alphabet Inc.’s debut Aussie dollar bond, expects more Big Tech issuance Down Under but cautions the market probably has only room for “a couple” such mega deals a year.

general.title: ECB Says Consumers’ Inflation Expectations Edged Down in July
general.summary: Inflation expectations among euro-area consumers inched down in July, easing European Central Bank concern over price risks from the Iran war.

general.title: Euro-Zone Business Activity Edges Up on Manufacturing Surge
general.summary: Private-sector activity in the euro area unexpectedly improved slightly in August, thanks to the strongest manufacturing growth in more than four years.

general.title: German Manufacturers See Best Month Since 2022 as Economy Heals
general.summary: Germany’s manufacturing sector recorded its best performance in more than four years in August, helping overall business activity expand for a second straight month.

general.title: Labubu maker Pop Mart shares fall as key ex-China sales data drop, Citi cuts price target
general.summary: Pop Mart shares fall after announcing first-half earnings.

general.title: India Banks’ Funding Costs Rise as RBI Ends Deposit Window Early
general.summary: Short-term borrowing costs for Indian lenders climbed most in a month after the nation’s central bank said it would end its overseas deposit facility early, taking away a cheaper and more stable source of funding.

general.title: French Business Activity Unexpectedly Weakens on Heat Wave
general.summary: France’s private sector unexpectedly weakened this month as extreme summer temperatures took a toll on the services sector.

general.title: ECB Well Placed to Act on ‘Uncomfortable’ Inflation, Kazaks Says
general.summary: The European Central Bank is well placed if further action is needed to return inflation to target from its current “somewhat uncomfortable” level, according to Governing Council member Martins Kazaks.

general.title: Stevenage Braces for Life After GSK as Drugmaker Moves to Cambridge
general.summary: Nursing a pint at a pub a short walk from GSK Plc’s research headquarters in Stevenage, 30 miles north of London, Paul Jamison is fretting about the British drugmaker’s campus becoming a wasteland. The town’s largest employer is leaving, with the majority of its 1,800 scientists and support staff moving to Cambridge.

general.title: UK Retail Sales Drop for the First Time in Three Months
general.summary: UK retail sales fell for the first time since April as scorching weather and fewer discounts discouraged shoppers and ended a recent rebound in consumer spending.

general.title: Surprise UK Deficit Shows Limits for Healey in First Budget
general.summary: Britain posted a surprise budget deficit in July, underscoring the fragile state of the public finances as Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey begins to draw up his crucial autumn budget.

general.title: Musk Touts Starlink for India’s Rural Users Amid Stalled Launch
general.summary: Billionaire Elon Musk pitched Starlink Inc.’s satellite-based internet service as a solution for India’s most underserved rural regions, even though the operator’s launch remains stalled in the country over security concerns.

general.title: UK Firms in Distress Rises 9% Led By Consumer-Facing Sectors
general.summary: The number of UK firms in critical financial distress grew by 9% in the past year, with consumer-facing industries coming under the most strain, according to research from financial and real estate advisory group BTG.

general.title: Fujifilm Expands Key Chip Material Output to Capture AI Demand
general.summary: Fujifilm Holdings Corp. is expanding production of key materials used in advanced semiconductor manufacturing to capitalize on surging demand.

general.title: Can Anthropic Beat SpaceX’s Record IPO Size?
general.summary: Anthropic expects to match or beat the size of SpaceX’s record-setting initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, in the latest sign of overwhelming demand from investors looking to profit from the artificial intelligence boom. Anthony Stephens has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Making Battlefield Tech Fuels an 80% Rally for Swedish Stock
general.summary: A small Swedish firm is Europe’s best-performing defense stock in 2026, an ascent its chief executive puts down to a “third wave” of military spending that’s focused more on computer systems and drones than tanks and ammunition.
